title: Indirect DNA extraction method suitable for acidic soil with high clay content
author: Högfors-Rönnholm, Christel, et al.

steps.title: Weigh soil into beaker
steps.instruction: Weigh 1.8 g of homogenized fresh clay soil into a sterile 100 mL beaker that contains a sterile magnetic stirring bar; cover the beaker with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Add sodium phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL of sodium phosphate buffer (soil : buffer ratio 1 : 1.5) to the beaker.

steps.title: Stir slurry first time
steps.instruction: Stir the slurry for 5 minutes at 250 rpm.

steps.title: Chill slurry
steps.instruction: Place the beaker on ice (or a 4 °C block) and chill for 3 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Stir slurry second time
steps.instruction: Stir the slurry again for 5 minutes at 250 rpm.

steps.title: Transfer and vortex slurry
steps.instruction: Transfer the slurry to a sterile 50 mL tube and vortex for 15 seconds.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 500 g for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pour the supernatant into a separate sterile 50 mL tube and store it in the dark at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet and repeat extraction
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL fresh sodium phosphate buffer to the pellet, suspend it by repeated pipetting with a 5 mL pipette, return the slurry to the beaker, and repeat steps 3–8 two additional times (total of three extractions).

substeps.instruction: Add 12 mL fresh sodium phosphate buffer to the pellet.
Suspend pellet by repeated pipetting with a 5 mL pipette.
Transfer slurry back to the beaker.
Repeat stirring (5 min, 250 rpm), chilling (3 min, 4 °C), stirring (5 min, 250 rpm), transfer, vortex, centrifuge, and supernatant collection two more times.

steps.title: Combine supernatants and discard pellet
steps.instruction: Collect all supernatants in the same 50 mL tube and discard the final soil pellet.

steps.title: Pellet cells from supernatant
steps.instruction: Divide the pooled supernatant (≈30 mL) into sterile 2.0 mL tubes and centrifuge at 10,000 g for 15 minutes to pellet the cells; extracellular DNA remains in the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the pooled supernatant into sterile 2.0 mL tubes.

steps.title: Wash cell pellets
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatants, pool the cell pellets into a 2.0 mL tube, and add 1 mL sodium phosphate buffer to wash away residual extracellular DNA.

substeps.instruction: Pool all cell pellets into a single 2.0 mL tube.
Add 1 mL sodium phosphate buffer and mix gently.

steps.title: Final pellet centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the washed pellet at 10,000 g for 15 minutes and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Extract DNA with kit
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell pellet to the bead tube of a commercial DNA isolation kit (e.g., DNeasy PowerSoil Kit) using the kit’s bead‑tube buffer, then perform DNA extraction according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

substeps.instruction: Move pellet to the kit’s bead tube.
Follow the kit protocol for DNA purification.

steps.title: Proceed to downstream analyses
steps.instruction: Use the indirectly extracted DNA for the intended downstream applications (e.g., PCR, sequencing).

description: Co-extraction of both intracellular DNA from living bacterial cells and extracellular DNA (eDNA) from dead cells by using standard direct DNA extraction methods can result in a considerable overestimation of the current, living microbial community in soil [1]. When working with clay rich soils, it is important to take into consideration that clay particles are known to preserve extracellular gene sequences due to their strong adsorptive binding of nucleic acids [2] as well as nucleases [3]. Therefore, if you do not separate the intact bacterial cells from the eDNA bound to the clay particles prior to DNA extraction, the subsequent high-throughput DNA sequencing will not be able to discriminate current and living bacterial species from remnant species no longer inhabiting the soil. This will thereby result in a skewed picture of the soil biodiversity [1]. In this paper, a modified indirect DNA extraction method based on a procedure for the separate recovery of intra- and extracellular DNA from marine samples by Alawi et al. [4] is described. The method uses a sodium phosphate buffer for the simultaneous release of both eDNA and bacterial cells from the soil. The method has further been optimized for acidic clay soil by adjusting the soil to buffer ratio, improving the separation procedure, and increasing the sodium phosphate buffer concentration [5] to increase cell yields. Only separated, intact bacterial cells are used for the subsequent DNA extraction and thereby, downstream analyses will only take into consideration the current, living microbial community. 1.The autoclaved sodium phosphate buffer is best stored in room temperature as it quickly crystallizes in lower temperatures.2.If soil samples with higher salt concentrations are used, 2% NaCl can be added to the sodium phosphate buffer to reduce the osmotic stress on the bacterial cells.3.Sometimes the final cell pellet after the washing step (points 12–13 in the protocol) can be hard and difficult to suspend
